By Dr. Sakshi Jain
 Your anterior (front tooth) composite filling has been completed using a tooth-colored restorative material designed to restore the appearance, function, and strength of your tooth. Following these instructions will help ensure the longevity of your restoration.

Immediately After the Procedure
* If local anesthesia was administered, avoid biting your lips, cheeks, or tongue until the numbness completely wears off (usually 2–4 hours).
* Since composite fillings harden immediately with the curing light, you can generally eat once the numbness has subsided.
Eating & Drinking
* Avoid very hard foods (such as ice, hard candies, or nuts) on the treated tooth for the first 24 hours.
* Limit foods and beverages that may stain the restoration, such as coffee, tea, red wine, turmeric-rich foods, and tobacco products, especially during the first 24–48 hours.
* Maintain good hydration and rinse your mouth with water after consuming staining foods or drinks.
 Oral Hygiene

* Brush twice daily using a soft-bristled toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste.
* Floss gently around the restored tooth every day.
* Good oral hygiene helps prevent decay around the edges of the filling and maintains its appearance.
* Mild sensitivity to hot, cold, or pressure is common for a few days and usually resolves on its own.

For patients who grind their teeth at night, a custom-made mouth guard can help prevent tooth wear, cracks, enamel damage, jaw pain, and headaches. It creates a protective barrier between the upper and lower teeth, reducing pressure on the teeth and jaw muscles.

🦷 Post Extraction Tips for a Smooth Recovery 🦷
By Dr. Sakshi Jain | Vital Dental Clinic

Getting a tooth removed can feel uncomfortable, but proper care after extraction helps you heal faster and avoid complications. Here are some simple and important tips to follow after your tooth extraction:

✅ Bite gently on the gauze pad for 30–45 minutes to control bleeding. Slight oozing is normal for a few hours.

✅ Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using a straw for the first 24 hours. This can disturb the blood clot and delay healing.

✅ Take prescribed medicines exactly as advised by your dentist. Do not skip painkillers or antibiotics if prescribed.

✅ Eat soft and cool foods like curd, khichdi, soup, smoothies, mashed potatoes, or ice cream. Avoid spicy, hot, crunchy, or hard foods for a few days.

✅ Apply an ice pack on the cheek for 10–15 minutes at a time to reduce swelling.

✅ Do not smoke or drink alcohol after extraction, as it slows healing and increases infection risk.

✅ Maintain oral hygiene carefully. Brush gently and avoid the extraction area for the first day. After 24 hours, rinse gently with warm salt water 2–3 times daily.

⚠️ Contact your dentist immediately if you experience severe pain, excessive bleeding, swelling, fever, or bad taste from the extraction site.
